title: Sukarno's birth chart
metaDescription: Sukarno's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 14.8° Gemini. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Four of the nine placements whose signs are settled stand in Gemini — the Sun, Venus, Neptune and Pluto. The placements whose signs could change with an unknown hour are not counted. A cluster that size becomes the section the rest of the chart plays around.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's exact place is 14.8° Gemini. That falls in the second decan, 10°–20°, sub-ruled by Venus in the classical scheme — a air sign read through a mutable season.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: The personal planets sit Mercury at 6.7° Cancer, Venus at 24.4° Gemini, Mars at 10.5° Virgo. Mercury in a water sign reads as a mind that absorbs before it argues; Venus in a air sign reads as taste led by wit and proportion; Mars in a earth sign reads as drive that grinds rather than flares.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The Sun and Uranus hold the closest angle here — an opposition, 0.1° wide. Across the wheel, each body sees the other in full. The old reading is not conflict so much as permanent mutual visibility. Behind it, Mars trine Jupiter at 0.6°, and Uranus opposition Pluto at 2.2° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: The Sun opposes Uranus while both square Mars. Two squares braced against one opposition make a t-square — the chart’s working end, where pressure keeps finding the same outlet. The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Two planets here sit in a sign the classical scheme scores. Jupiter in Capricorn at 11.1° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Saturn in Capricorn at 15.1° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Among the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the elements divide 4 air, 3 earth, 1 water, 1 fire; by modality, 6 mutable, 3 cardinal. Air weights a chart toward language and pattern — the impulse to name a thing before deciding how to feel about it. Jupiter, Saturn and Uranus were retrograde — apparent retreat against the stars, which the old reading takes as a function working from the inside first.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Capricorn into Aquarius during that day at the birthplace, travelling 12.9° between one midnight and the next. The hour would decide it; no hour was recorded. The reading keeps the question open rather than flipping a coin dressed as astrology.
